items.title: Google DeepMind integrates computer use into Gemini 3.5 Flash to enable cross-platform agent interactions and improve enterprise automation tasks [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Introducing computer use in Gemini 3.5 Flash
items.summary:
Google DeepMind has integrated computer use directly into its Gemini 3.5 Flash model, enhancing its ability to build agents that operate across browser, mobile, and desktop platforms. This integration improves performance on complex, long-term tasks such as continuous software testing and enterprise automation, allowing agents to see, reason, and act within various professional applications. The feature is accessible through the Gemini API and Enterprise Agent Platform, enabling developers and enterprises to create more capable and versatile AI agents.

To ensure safety in live environments, DeepMind has implemented targeted adversarial training and introduced optional enterprise safeguards that require user confirmation for sensitive actions and can halt tasks if prompt injection is detected. These measures, combined with recommended practices like sandboxing and human oversight, aim to mitigate risks associated with autonomous agent operation. Early users have reported positive outcomes, highlighting the practical benefits of this new capability.

items.title: OpenAI unveils Jalapeño, its first custom inference chip built by Broadcom to optimize AI model performance and reduce operating costs [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
items.originalTitle: OpenAI unveils its first custom chip, built by Broadcom
items.summary:
OpenAI has introduced Jalapeño, its first custom inference chip developed in partnership with Broadcom to enhance AI model performance and reduce operating costs. The chip is tailored specifically for OpenAI's inference workloads, with early tests indicating improved performance-per-watt compared to existing solutions. This move aims to optimize real-time AI model execution, particularly for coding tasks, while potentially lowering dependence on Nvidia GPUs.

The collaboration, announced in October, reflects OpenAI's strategy to design infrastructure components such as chip architecture and deployment systems alongside its AI models. By creating purpose-built hardware, OpenAI seeks to improve speed, reliability, and affordability across its AI services, marking a significant step in the company's efforts to control the entire technology stack supporting its models.

items.title: RubyLLM launches a unified Ruby framework supporting all major AI providers with features for chatbots, AI agents, image generation, transcription, and more [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: RubyLLM: A Ruby framework for all major AI providers
items.summary:
RubyLLM has introduced a unified Ruby framework that supports all major AI providers, enabling developers to build chatbots, AI agents, image generation tools, transcription services, and various AI workflows with a consistent interface. The framework simplifies integration by replacing multiple provider-specific clients with a single, lightweight solution compatible with platforms like OpenAI, Anthropic, and others.

The framework offers features such as conversational AI, vision analysis, audio transcription, document extraction, image generation, embeddings, content moderation, and tool integration. It supports real-time streaming responses, structured JSON output, and Rails integration, making it versatile for different AI applications. RubyLLM aims to streamline AI development in Ruby by providing a comprehensive, easy-to-use toolkit that handles diverse AI tasks within one cohesive environment.

items.title: Krea releases Krea 2, a 12-billion-parameter open-weight image generation model focused on aesthetic diversity and creative control [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Krea 2: SOTA open-weights 12B image model
items.summary:
Krea has released Krea 2, a 12-billion-parameter open-weight image generation model designed to enhance aesthetic diversity and creative control for users. The model employs a multi-stage training pipeline and innovative architecture to support broad stylistic exploration and precise user guidance through both text and image inputs. Krea 2 aims to serve as a foundation for creative image generation, balancing high performance with flexibility in visual expression.

The development of Krea 2 involved building a large-scale data infrastructure and distributed training framework to curate a diverse dataset covering wide-ranging styles and world knowledge. The model incorporates advanced techniques such as diffusion transformers, improved VAEs, and novel attention mechanisms to improve training efficiency and output quality. Additionally, Krea 2 includes a prompt expander and style-reference system to help users navigate and control the model's extensive visual space more effectively.

Krea 2 ranks among the top models on the Artificial Analysis leaderboard for text-to-image generation, reflecting its competitive performance and creative potential. By focusing on exploratory generation rather than a single default aesthetic, Krea 2 offers users practical tools to experiment with styles, moods, and compositions, supporting a more versatile and expressive creative process.

items.title: Writer argues against labeling all content as AI-generated, urging distinction between AI-assisted and human-created work to preserve meaningful critique and support for authors [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Calling everything AI-generated is lazy
items.summary:
The article critiques the widespread habit of labeling all written content as AI-generated, arguing that this oversimplification undermines meaningful critique and unfairly targets human authors. It calls for a clearer distinction between content genuinely produced by AI and work that is human-created but may use AI tools for assistance, such as proofreading or language improvement.

The author highlights how dismissive comments accusing posts of being AI-generated offer no constructive feedback and can discourage genuine writers, especially those who use AI tools to enhance clarity without compromising authenticity. Emphasizing the value of personal experience and accountability in writing, the article urges readers to focus on the substance and accuracy of content rather than making unfounded assumptions about its origin.

By advocating for more precise language and understanding in discussions about AI and writing, the article warns against the negative impact of blanket accusations on individual creators and encourages support for authentic, thoughtful contributions in the digital space.

items.title: CelestoAI releases SmolFS, a durable filesystem layer for AI agents supporting local and cloud storage with Python and TypeScript SDKs [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Show HN: A durable filesystem layer for AI agents
items.summary:
CelestoAI has launched SmolFS, a durable filesystem layer tailored for AI agents that supports both local and cloud storage. It provides persistent workspace folders that remain accessible across agent process restarts, enhancing data reliability in AI workflows. SmolFS includes Python and TypeScript SDKs, allowing seamless integration without requiring agents to manage storage details directly.

SmolFS offers a unified command-line interface for managing storage lifecycle tasks such as creating volumes, mounting, flushing, and unmounting. It supports local development with SQLite-backed volumes and cloud deployments using Redis for metadata and S3-compatible object storage for file contents. This design enables AI agents to maintain state across sessions and share workspaces across different runtimes efficiently.

By explicitly managing cloud credentials and storage configurations, SmolFS facilitates easier auditing and secure handling of durable agent data. Its lightweight SDKs and managed backend simplify the developer experience, making it a practical solution for persistent storage needs in AI applications.

items.title: Grab develops Palana, a Kubernetes-native platform to securely run autonomous AI agents with infrastructure-level safeguards and zero-trust isolation [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
items.originalTitle: Grab Builds Secure Agentic AI Workload Platform
items.summary:
Grab's security and platform engineering teams have developed Palana, a Kubernetes-native platform designed to securely run autonomous AI agents by implementing infrastructure-level safeguards. Palana addresses the unpredictable and potentially risky behaviors of model-driven agents through isolated namespaces, strict role-based access controls, and proxy-mediated secrets management, ensuring zero-trust isolation and operational auditability.

The platform uses dedicated Kubernetes namespaces with restrictive policies to isolate each agent, preventing security breaches from affecting other workloads or the underlying cluster. Sensitive credentials are protected by HashiCorp Vault and dynamically injected via a secure proxy, eliminating exposure within the agent runtime. All outbound traffic is routed through a centralized proxy with real-time inspection and policy enforcement, while external controls manage agent lifecycle and network access independently from the agents themselves.

By integrating with Kubernetes-native tools and infrastructure-as-code practices, Palana enables scalable, auditable management of numerous concurrent AI agent workloads. This approach provides a systematic, secure environment for deploying autonomous AI applications, mitigating risks such as prompt injection, logic hijacking, and unauthorized access inherent in agentic AI systems.

items.originalTitle: TronBrowser is an open-source, privacy-first, AI-native web browser
items.summary:
TronBrowser is a new open-source web browser built on Ungoogled Chromium that prioritizes user privacy by eliminating telemetry, ads, and sponsored tabs. It features a built-in AI sidebar that supports multiple AI models through user-provided keys and offers a command-line interface for enhanced control. The browser maintains compatibility with Chrome extensions and allows users to manage their own data, either locally or via cloud services.

Designed to provide a secure and customizable browsing experience, TronBrowser is free under the MIT License and supports integration with AI services such as Anthropic's Claude, OpenAI's GPT, and Google's Gemini. It also enables users to run local AI models and self-host services, distinguishing itself from other browsers by removing Google phone-home functionality and affiliate link injections.

items.title: ProductNow.ai blog says AI-assisted development has shifted the engineering bottleneck from writing code to deciding what to write and catching subtle errors [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: The engineering bottleneck has moved
items.summary:
The ProductNow.ai blog highlights a significant shift in software engineering caused by AI-assisted development. Traditionally, engineers focused heavily on making the right design decisions early, as mistakes were costly and difficult to reverse. However, with AI tools making code writing and refactoring faster and cheaper, the main challenge has moved to deciding what to write, identifying subtle errors, and exercising sound judgment.

The blog explains that AI has reduced the cost and risk associated with changes like dependency updates and code cleanup, allowing engineers to experiment and iterate more freely. This shift encourages a more exploratory approach to design and development, where caution is reserved for decisions that are truly hard to reverse, such as data migrations or external API contracts. Overall, AI is transforming engineering workflows by making code modification less burdensome and emphasizing decision-making quality over initial code creation.

items.title: Promptctl launches as a Git-like tool for versioning, diffing, and rolling back AI prompts to improve prompt management and collaboration [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Show HN: Promptctl – Git for your AI prompts
items.summary:
Promptctl is a new tool designed to manage AI prompts with version control features similar to Git. It enables users to track, version, compare, and roll back changes to their AI prompts, improving organization and collaboration in prompt development. This tool addresses common challenges such as scattered prompt storage and difficulty in tracking changes or reverting to previous versions.

Promptctl supports various commands for initializing projects, committing prompt versions, viewing history, comparing versions, and rolling back changes. It also offers features like tagging prompts by model, searching across prompts, exporting version histories, and automatically committing changes from files. The tool aims to bring structured version management to AI prompt workflows, enhancing reproducibility and ease of maintenance.

Unlike traditional browser automation tools that launch fresh browsers requiring re-login and often trigger bot detection, chrome-use operates within the user's existing Chrome environment, making it indistinguishable from human browsing activity. It is compatible with various AI agents and command-line interfaces, providing a flexible and stealthy solution for browser automation that maintains all existing cookies, sessions, and browser fingerprints. Installation is straightforward via a script that downloads prebuilt binaries and sets up the necessary extension, with additional AI agent skills available for integration.

items.title: Halyard launches open-source AI work ledger for developers to track time, token usage, costs, and generate client-safe invoices locally without cloud or accounts [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Halyard – open AI work ledger for developers (time, tokens, cost, invoices)
items.summary:
Halyard is an open-source AI work ledger designed for developers to track time, token usage, costs, and generate client-safe invoices locally without relying on cloud services or accounts. It captures AI session metadata such as time, tokens, model, and project details in plain-text logs stored on the user's machine, ensuring privacy by never recording prompt content or code. The tool integrates with various AI platforms and editors, providing cost breakdowns, project attribution, and invoice evidence through local reports and dashboards.

Halyard targets individual developers, freelancers, small AI teams, and enterprises by offering a transparent and auditable way to manage AI-assisted work expenses and outputs. Its features include lightweight hooks for automatic session capture, analytics for cost allocation, and proof artifacts that can be shared with clients without exposing sensitive data. The project is currently in alpha and licensed under MIT, emphasizing user ownership and privacy.

items.title: M5Stack launches StackChan AI desktop robot with ESP32-S3 CoreS3 controller, 2-inch touch display, camera, sensors, servos, RGB LEDs, NFC, and programmable via Arduino and UiFlow2 [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: M5StackChan AI Desktop Robot
items.summary:
M5Stack has introduced StackChan, an AI desktop robot featuring the CoreS3 controller based on the ESP32-S3 SoC. The robot includes a 2-inch capacitive touch display, a camera, multiple sensors, servos for movement, RGB LEDs, NFC, and supports programming through Arduino and UiFlow2. It is designed as a versatile AI companion with capabilities such as voice interaction, smart home control, and IoT integration.

StackChan's hardware integrates a 240 MHz dual-core processor, 16MB Flash, 8MB PSRAM, Wi-Fi, BLE, and various sensors including a 9-axis IMU and proximity sensor. The robot body contains servos for horizontal and vertical movement, RGB lighting, infrared communication, a touch panel, and a rechargeable battery. Its firmware offers features like AI agent functionality, expressive animations, wireless remote control, and OTA updates.

The device supports multiple development platforms and can connect to other M5Stack expansion units, enabling users to customize and extend its functions. StackChan aims to serve as a desktop companion and AI assistant, with community contributions helping to enhance its capabilities and user experience.

items.title: Anthropic Claude Code lead argues HTML improves human-agent communication and engagement over Markdown in complex agentic workflows [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Anthropic Lead: HTML Increasingly Better Than Markdown at Keeping Humans Engaged in Agentic Loops
items.summary:
Thariq Shihipar, engineering lead for Anthropic's Claude Code team, argues that HTML enhances human-agent communication and engagement more effectively than Markdown in complex workflows. He highlights HTML's richer visualizations, interactivity, and color as key factors that improve productivity, especially in tasks involving goal communication, specification refinement, and output review.

Shihipar points out that as agent outputs grow longer and more complex, Markdown becomes restrictive and harder to read, leading to potential quality and maintenance issues if outputs are accepted without thorough review. He advocates for single-file HTML artifacts that create interactive, customized workspaces suited to various tasks such as code review, interface design, and data visualization. This perspective has sparked debate among developers, with some supporting HTML's advantages and others cautioning against losing Markdown's simplicity and security benefits.

items.title: Google rolls out new Search Services History feature storing uploaded media for AI training by default; users can opt out via My Activity settings
items.originalTitle: How to Opt Out of Google Search’s New AI Data Training Feature
items.summary:
Google has introduced a new Search Services History feature that automatically stores media uploads, such as images and audio from user interactions, to train its AI models. This update is part of a global rollout and is enabled by default, though users can opt out through the My Activity settings by disabling the option to save media for AI training.

The stored media includes a wide range of content, from photos used in reverse image searches to voice recordings from Google Translate, and is retained for up to four years even if users delete the original activity. Google states that these settings aim to provide more relevant search results and allow users to revisit past searches, but the default opt-in approach has raised privacy concerns among experts who advocate for explicit user consent before data collection for AI training.

items.title: OpenAI and Broadcom announce Jalapeño chip for large language model inference, targeting data center deployment by end of 2026 [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: OpenAI and Broadcom announce chip designed for LLM inference at scale
items.summary:
OpenAI and Broadcom have jointly announced the Jalapeño chip, a new application-specific integrated circuit designed specifically for large language model (LLM) inference in data centers. The chip aims to improve performance and energy efficiency for LLM workloads and is expected to be deployed in data centers by the end of 2026. This initiative represents the first generation of a long-term project to develop specialized hardware tailored to OpenAI's evolving model requirements.

Broadcom developed the chip based on detailed insights from OpenAI's research and roadmap, completing the design and production in nine months. Early testing indicates that Jalapeño offers substantially better performance per watt compared to current state-of-the-art solutions, although a detailed technical report is forthcoming. This collaboration reflects OpenAI's strategy to reduce reliance on external suppliers like Nvidia by owning more of its technology stack and addresses the growing demand for compute capacity amid a global shortage in data center resources.

items.title: Cerebras shares drop nearly 20% after Q1 earnings as CEO says investors misunderstood narrower full-year gross margin guidance [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Cerebras stock plunges after earnings as CEO says margin outlook was misunderstood
items.summary:
Shares of AI chipmaker Cerebras Systems fell nearly 20% following its first quarterly earnings report since going public, despite better-than-expected results. The company forecasted a narrower full-year gross margin of 38% to 41%, down from the 47% reported in Q1, which caused investor concern. CEO Andrew Feldman clarified that the margin guidance was misunderstood, explaining that the company plans to rent back equipment from a major customer temporarily to increase capacity while building its own data center, impacting profit margins this year.

Cerebras reported $193 million in revenue for the quarter, a 94% increase year-over-year, and narrowed its net loss to $14 million from $23.9 million the previous year. The stock decline brought its price close to the IPO level, reflecting market apprehension about the margin outlook despite strong revenue growth and improved earnings performance.

items.title: Jim Mont explores how large language model code style choices impact token costs and efficiency, highlighting trade-offs between readability and API pricing [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: What I'm Finding About LLM Code Style and Token Costs
items.summary:
Jim Mont examines how coding styles generated by large language models (LLMs) affect token consumption and API costs, emphasizing the trade-offs between code readability and efficiency. He highlights that many LLM-generated code patterns are longer and less optimized, leading to higher token usage and increased expenses, especially as output tokens are priced significantly higher than input tokens.

Mont points out that modern runtimes like Deno and Cloudflare Workers natively support web APIs, which can reduce the need for verbose or legacy code patterns that LLMs often default to due to their training on older Node.js codebases. By aligning code generation with these native APIs, developers can minimize token costs and improve code efficiency.

The article underscores the economic impact of coding style choices in LLM-assisted development and encourages awareness of platform capabilities to optimize token usage. Mont's insights aim to help developers balance practical coding conventions with cost-effective API usage in evolving web environments.

Jim Mont examines how coding styles generated by large language models (LLMs) affect token consumption and API costs, emphasizing the trade-offs between code readability and efficiency. He highlights that many LLM-generated code patterns are longer and less optimized, leading to higher token usage and increased expenses, especially as output tokens are priced significantly higher than input tokens.

Mont points out that modern runtimes like Deno and Cloudflare Workers natively support web APIs, which can reduce the need for verbose or legacy code patterns that LLMs often default to due to their training on older Node.js codebases. By aligning code generation with these native APIs, developers can minimize token costs and improve code efficiency.

The article underscores the economic impact of coding style choices in LLM-assisted development and encourages awareness of platform capabilities to optimize token usage. Mont's insights aim to help developers balance practical coding conventions with cost-effective API usage in evolving web environments.

items.title: A24 announces $75 million AI research partnership with Google DeepMind amid backlash from indie film fans [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: A24 Knows You’re Mad About the Google AI Collab
items.summary:
A24, the influential indie film studio known for hits like "Backrooms," has announced a $75 million research partnership with Google DeepMind to develop new AI filmmaking tools. This collaboration, part of A24's technology startup A24 Labs, aims to give artists a role in shaping AI-driven creative workflows. The announcement has sparked backlash among A24's dedicated fanbase, who view the move as contradictory to the studio's indie ethos and have expressed their discontent on social media.

The partnership reflects a broader trend of AI companies increasing their presence in Hollywood, raising concerns about AI's impact on creative jobs and the film industry. While some studios have embraced AI investments, others have faced criticism and legal challenges over copyright issues. A24 emphasizes that the collaboration is a research effort intended to influence the development of AI tools rather than passively adopting existing technologies, seeking to maintain a voice for artists in the evolving landscape.

items.title: SignalFire data shows engineering jobs are the most resilient in tech hiring during 2025 despite AI-driven layoff narratives [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: AI was supposed to kill engineering jobs, but new data suggests they’re the most resilient
items.summary:
Despite widespread narratives that AI is driving layoffs in tech, new data from venture firm SignalFire reveals that engineering jobs remain the most resilient in the industry during 2025. SignalFire's analysis shows that while overall tech hiring declined by 25% compared to 2019, engineering roles only saw an 11% drop, and engineers accounted for 55% of new hires at major tech companies, up from 46% in 2019. Early-stage startups also increased their engineering hires by 7% over the same period.

This trend suggests that AI has not reduced demand for engineering talent; instead, it appears to have increased productivity and expanded the scope of work for engineers. Industry leaders, including Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang, have noted that AI tools are making engineers busier rather than replacing them. SignalFire's findings challenge the assumption that AI will lead to widespread job losses among software engineers, highlighting a more complex relationship between automation and workforce dynamics in tech.

items.originalTitle: AI researchers continue to leave Google for its rivals
items.summary:
Top AI researchers Jonas Adler and Alexander Pritzel are leaving Google to join Anthropic, continuing a recent wave of departures from Google's AI team. Both played significant roles in developing Google's Gemini model, and their moves follow the exits of notable scientists Noam Shazeer, who joined OpenAI, and John Jumper, who also moved to Anthropic.

These departures highlight a growing trend as competitors like OpenAI and Anthropic prepare for public offerings, attracting top talent with equity incentives. The shifts raise concerns about Google's ability to retain leading AI researchers amid increasing competition in the industry.

items.title: OpenAI and Broadcom unveil Jalapeño, a custom LLM inference chip promising improved performance per watt and scalable deployment starting in 2026 [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
items.originalTitle: OpenAI and Broadcom unveil LLM-optimized inference chip
items.summary:
OpenAI and Broadcom have jointly unveiled Jalapeño, a custom-designed AI inference chip optimized for large language models (LLMs). Developed in just nine months, Jalapeño aims to deliver significantly improved performance per watt compared to current state-of-the-art accelerators, supporting scalable deployment in data centers starting in 2026. This chip represents a key part of OpenAI's strategy to build a full-stack platform encompassing models, products, and hardware infrastructure.

Jalapeño was designed from the ground up based on OpenAI's deep understanding of LLM inference requirements, with Broadcom contributing expertise in silicon implementation and networking technologies. Early testing indicates the chip achieves high efficiency by balancing compute, memory, and networking resources, enabling it to run advanced AI workloads such as GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark at production target frequencies and power. The collaboration is set to support gigawatt-scale deployments with partners including Microsoft, marking a multi-generation roadmap to accelerate AI performance and accessibility.

items.title: WIRED reports China’s top AI experts express concern over AI arms race risks amid calls for US-China cooperation to prevent catastrophic failures [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: I Met With China’s Top AI Experts. They’re Freaking Out, Too
items.summary:
At a recent AI conference in Beijing, leading experts from China and the US highlighted the risks of an AI arms race and emphasized the need for cooperation to prevent catastrophic failures. They warned that as AI systems become more advanced and autonomous, the potential for cyberattacks and systemic failures grows, making collaboration between the two AI superpowers essential for global safety.

The conference underscored that while the US has imposed restrictions on China's AI development due to national security concerns, both countries share common interests in managing AI risks. Experts pointed to the benefits of international collaboration, drawing parallels to past cooperation on nuclear safety despite geopolitical tensions. They also discussed challenges related to open-weight AI models, which are crucial for innovation but pose security risks if not properly managed.

Participants stressed the importance of developing shared safety standards and technical measures to mitigate risks without compromising sensitive information. The consensus was that balancing openness with security and fostering dialogue between nations will be critical to ensuring AI advances do not lead to unintended, potentially disastrous consequences.

This shift follows an earlier phase where firms encouraged heavy AI usage to maximize budgets, but now they face challenges in managing expenses and ensuring value from AI investments.

Accenture has reportedly taken steps to limit AI use for simple activities such as converting PDFs into presentations, after previously urging employees to adopt AI to enhance performance. Internal discussions highlight concerns from leadership about the growing and unpredictable costs associated with AI, prompting a reevaluation of spending strategies as the industry moves from initial excitement to demonstrating tangible business value.

items.summary:
Rep. She emphasized that all official bill text originates from the House Legislative Council, which is prohibited from using AI in its drafting process. Luna's statement came after social media posts suggested AI had been used to write parts of the amendment, prompting her to correct the record and stress that no legislation is drafted with AI.

The incident highlights ongoing concerns about the role of AI in legislative and legal processes, as AI tools become more prevalent in various professional settings. While some lawmakers have experimented with AI for drafting legislation, official procedures typically restrict its use to ensure accuracy and accountability. Luna's response underscores the importance of transparency and adherence to established protocols in legislative drafting amid increasing AI adoption.

items.title: Uber, DoorDash, and Cloudflare expand AI use from code review to product requirement validation and governance, introducing AI-driven evaluation layers across the software development lifecycle [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: AI Is Moving up the Software Lifecycle: From Code Review to PRD Governance
items.summary:
Technology companies Uber, DoorDash, and Cloudflare are expanding the use of artificial intelligence beyond code generation and review to earlier stages of the software development lifecycle, such as product requirement document (PRD) validation and design inputs. These initiatives introduce AI-driven governance layers that evaluate engineering artifacts before implementation, aiming to improve clarity, completeness, and risk assessment while maintaining human oversight.

Uber's AI system reviews PRDs to identify missing dependencies and unclear assumptions before engineering teams begin work. DoorDash employs an AI-powered code reviewer that provides actionable, context-aware feedback integrated into existing workflows to enhance review efficiency without increasing noise. Cloudflare uses a multi-agent AI approach, assigning specialized tasks like security and performance analysis to different agents, which collectively improve review precision and reduce false positives.

These developments reflect a broader trend of embedding AI as a first-pass evaluation tool across the software lifecycle, supporting continuous validation and refinement of software artifacts while preserving engineers' final decision-making authority.

items.title: Anthropic replaces CEO Dario Amodei with cofounder Tom Brown in White House talks amid export control discussions over Claude Fable 5 AI model [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: The Trump White House Is Over Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei
items.summary:
Anthropic has replaced CEO Dario Amodei with cofounder Tom Brown in recent discussions with the White House regarding the export controls on its Claude Fable 5 AI model. The change in representation comes amid ongoing talks about lifting restrictions that were imposed after concerns about the model's security and potential for misuse were raised by the National Security Agency.

The administration has engaged in multiple high-level and technical meetings with Anthropic, led by Brown and the company's public policy chief, Sarah Heck, who have been more receptive to government concerns than Amodei. While the timeline for redeploying Fable 5 remains uncertain, these discussions aim to establish criteria that could address the administration's worries about AI model jailbreaks and potentially lead to lifting the export controls.

These enhancements reflect Figma's focus on streamlining creative processes and fostering collaboration through intelligent automation and extensible tools.

items.title: OpenAI unveils Jalapeño, its first custom AI inference processor chip made with Broadcom, aiming to power large language models by 2026 [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: OpenAI reveals its first AI processor: Jalapeño
items.summary:
OpenAI has introduced Jalapeño, its first custom AI inference processor chip developed in collaboration with Broadcom. Designed specifically for AI inference tasks, Jalapeño aims to power current and future large language models, including those used by ChatGPT, with improved performance and energy efficiency. This marks a strategic move by OpenAI to reduce reliance on Nvidia GPUs, which are currently in limited supply.

Jalapeño is an application-specific integrated circuit (ASIC) tailored for processing AI model requests rather than training. Broadcom's CEO noted that the chip's performance is comparable to Nvidia's Blackwell chips and Google's Tensor processing units. OpenAI plans to deploy this multi-generation compute platform by the end of 2026, anticipating significant gains in performance per watt compared to existing technologies.

This development places OpenAI among other major tech companies like Microsoft, Meta, and Amazon, which have also launched custom AI chips to enhance their AI infrastructure. While these companies continue to compete in the AI chip market, OpenAI's Jalapeño represents a key step toward more efficient and scalable AI model deployment.

items.title: Qualcomm to acquire AI chip software startup Modular for nearly $4 billion, deal expected to close in second half of 2026 [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Qualcomm Buys Buzzy Chip Startup Modular for Nearly $4 Billion
items.summary:
Qualcomm announced its plan to acquire Modular, a Silicon Valley startup specializing in AI chip software, for nearly $4 billion. The deal, expected to close in the second half of 2026, involves issuing up to 19.2 million shares of Qualcomm common stock. Modular's technology includes a proprietary coding language that enables AI software to run across different chips without rewriting code, and its team of around 150 employees will join Qualcomm.

This acquisition reflects Qualcomm's strategy to expand beyond its core mobile device chip market into AI and data center technologies. Modular, founded in 2022 by industry veterans Chris Lattner and Tim Davis, has developed a platform that challenges existing GPU software systems by offering a more flexible, developer-friendly solution. Qualcomm's move aligns with its broader efforts to innovate in AI hardware and software integration, including previous acquisitions and partnerships in the data center space.

items.title: Technology Review reports on the emergence of a new web data infrastructure layer designed to provide real-time, scalable, and structured data access for AI applications amid growing enterprise demand [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: The emergence of the web data infrastructure layer for AI
items.summary:
As AI applications rapidly expand, enterprises face challenges in accessing the vast, dynamic, and often unstructured web data needed to power these technologies effectively. A new web data infrastructure layer is emerging to address this gap by enabling real-time, scalable, and structured data retrieval that supports AI models with fresh, relevant, and trustworthy information. This infrastructure aims to overcome the limitations of the web's original design, which was not built for automated data discovery and retrieval at the scale AI now demands.

This new layer integrates diverse data sources, including public web content, APIs, licensed datasets, and proprietary information, to provide a continuous feed of updated data tailored to specific contexts. By reducing latency and improving data quality, it helps prevent outdated or inaccurate AI outputs, thereby enhancing decision-making and user trust. Industry experts highlight that combining powerful AI models with robust, real-time data access is essential for the next phase of AI development and operational success.

items.title: Immunologist Derya Unutmaz uses GPT-5 Pro to solve a 3-year-old T cell glucose metabolism mystery, advancing cancer and autoimmune research [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: How GPT-5 helped immunologist Derya Unutmaz solve a 3-year-old mystery
items.summary:
Immunologist Derya Unutmaz used GPT-5 Pro to solve a three-year-old puzzle about how glucose affects T cell development, a key question in immunology with implications for cancer and autoimmune disease research. The AI model helped identify that a glucose-like molecule, deoxyglucose, disrupts the production of a protein that normally prevents T cells from becoming inflammatory cells, explaining unexpected experimental results.

Unutmaz's team initially struggled to interpret their findings from 2022, but GPT-5 Pro provided insights that connected glucose metabolism to T cell specialization. The model also accurately predicted outcomes of related experiments, demonstrating its potential as a collaborative tool in scientific research. This breakthrough highlights how advanced AI can augment human expertise and accelerate understanding in complex biomedical fields.

items.title: OpenAI helps found Appia Foundation to develop shared technical standards and evaluation frameworks for advanced AI safety and governance [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Helping build shared standards for advanced AI
items.summary:
OpenAI has co-founded the Appia Foundation, hosted by the Linux Foundation, to develop shared technical standards and evaluation frameworks aimed at enhancing the safety and governance of advanced AI systems. The foundation seeks to create open, modular specifications that translate international standards into practical assessment criteria, fostering trust and cooperation among organizations and governments worldwide.

This initiative builds on OpenAI's broader efforts to strengthen AI safety through rigorous evaluation practices and governance frameworks, including partnerships with U.S. and U.K. agencies. By promoting interoperable standards and trusted third-party assessments, the Appia Foundation aims to support coordinated responses to AI risks and facilitate global collaboration in managing the challenges posed by increasingly capable AI technologies.

items.title: Google advances AI-powered natural disaster forecasting and real-time alerts to improve global crisis resilience and reduce surprise from extreme weather events [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Towards a world where no one is surprised by a natural disaster
items.summary:
Google is advancing AI-powered technologies to improve natural disaster forecasting and provide real-time alerts, aiming to enhance global crisis resilience and reduce unexpected impacts from extreme weather events. Building on a decade of research, Google has developed models that predict floods, wildfires, earthquakes, and extreme weather with greater accuracy and lead time, reaching billions of people worldwide through its platforms.

Key innovations include a global flood forecasting model covering over 150 countries, AI-based wildfire boundary tracking in 34 countries, and the WeatherNext 2 system for detailed cyclone predictions. Google also collaborates with partners to deploy satellite constellations for wildfire detection and uses AI to help cities mitigate extreme heat. These efforts are integrated into Google Search, Maps, and public alert systems to deliver timely, authoritative crisis information to users and emergency responders.

items.title: Oracle lays off 21,000 employees amid $45 billion debt-fueled AI infrastructure investments for cloud expansion in fiscal 2026 [ ! ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Oracle’s 21,000 layoffs help drive its debt-fueled AI investments
items.summary:
Oracle has laid off 21,000 employees, reducing its workforce by nearly 13% as part of a restructuring plan linked to its significant investments in AI and cloud infrastructure. The company is raising $45 billion to $50 billion, largely through debt, to expand its Oracle Cloud Infrastructure to support AI workloads for clients including OpenAI and Meta. This move reflects Oracle's strategic shift toward AI-driven cloud services amid growing concerns about its rising debt and reliance on unprofitable AI customers.

The layoffs coincide with a $1.8 billion restructuring cost and follow reports of mass job cuts earlier in the year. Oracle acknowledged potential challenges from the workforce reduction, such as decreased productivity and loss of skilled employees, but emphasized its commitment to balancing resources to deliver advanced cloud and AI products. The company's approach illustrates how AI adoption can indirectly contribute to job reductions beyond direct automation, a trend increasingly cited by technology firms during workforce adjustments.

items.originalTitle: How Omio is building the future of conversational travel
items.summary:
Omio, a leading multimodal travel platform operating across 47 countries, is leveraging OpenAI's technology to revolutionize travel discovery and booking through conversational AI. By integrating OpenAI models with its transportation network, Omio enables travelers to plan and book trips via natural language conversations, connecting them to real-time transportation data from over 3,000 providers. This approach marks a shift from traditional search interfaces to AI-native customer experiences.

Beyond enhancing customer interactions, Omio has transformed its internal operations by adopting OpenAI tools like ChatGPT and Codex, significantly accelerating product development. The company reports that development time for new products has been reduced by 80%, allowing smaller teams to deliver projects faster and fostering greater experimentation. Omio aims to become fully AI-native by rethinking workflows across all functions, emphasizing responsible deployment throughout its AI integration.

items.title: Cory Doctorow discusses AI hype and economic risks in his new book The Reverse Centaur’s Guide to Life After AI [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: How to burst the AI bubble: Strike at its roots
items.summary:
Cory Doctorow, a science fiction author and tech journalist, explores the hype and economic risks surrounding artificial intelligence in his new book, The Reverse Centaur’s Guide to Life After AI. He critiques the AI industry's tendency to create roles where humans serve as mere extensions of machines, which he terms "reverse centaurs," and warns of the potential collapse of the AI investment bubble due to unsustainable spending on large AI models.

Doctorow distinguishes between beneficial AI augmentation and the problematic replacement of human roles with AI, highlighting concerns about unrealistic expectations and the financial instability of the AI sector. While not opposed to AI itself, he calls for a more grounded understanding of its capabilities and consequences, emphasizing the need to challenge prevailing narratives that drive excessive investment and hype in the technology.

items.title: AWS launches Blocks, an open-source TypeScript framework for AI agents to build and deploy backends locally and on AWS services in public preview [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: AWS Launches Blocks, an Open-Source TypeScript Framework Designed for AI Agents to Build Backends
items.summary:
AWS has launched Blocks, an open-source TypeScript framework currently in public preview, designed to help AI agents build and deploy backend applications both locally and on AWS services. Each Block packages application code, local mocks, and AWS infrastructure, enabling developers to run applications locally without an AWS account and deploy the same code seamlessly to services like Lambda, DynamoDB, Aurora, and Bedrock. The framework aims to simplify backend development by guiding AI-generated code toward correct architecture from the start.

Blocks offers a modular approach where each Block represents a backend capability such as databases, authentication, or real-time messaging. Developers can compose these Blocks, and the framework automatically generates AWS infrastructure following best practices. It supports a local-first development model with hot reload and type safety that extends from backend to frontend across various web and native frameworks. Blocks integrates with AWS CDK, allowing customization and embedding within existing infrastructure stacks.

Positioned as complementary to AWS Amplify, Blocks focuses on type-safe infrastructure code and local development, assuming AI agents write the code. Around 20 Blocks are available covering core backend services, with no extra charge beyond AWS service usage. The framework is available across all commercial AWS regions under the Apache 2.0 license, though it remains in preview with some evolving features and requirements.

items.title: OpenAI launches Daybreak tools including Codex Security and GPT-5.5-Cyber to automate vulnerability discovery and patching for organizations worldwide [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
items.originalTitle: Daybreak: Tools for securing every organization in the world
items.summary:
OpenAI has launched Daybreak, a suite of tools including Codex Security and GPT-5.5-Cyber, designed to automate the discovery, validation, and patching of software vulnerabilities for organizations worldwide. These tools aim to accelerate end-to-end patch automation, helping defenders manage the increasing volume of vulnerabilities found by AI models.

Daybreak includes an updated Codex Security plugin that integrates lessons from internal and customer use to speed up vulnerability management and prevention. The full version of GPT-5.5-Cyber, now available to trusted defenders, improves performance on cybersecurity tasks. Additionally, the Daybreak Cyber Partner Program and the Patch the Planet initiative collaborate with open-source projects and security partners to scale these capabilities and ensure responsible access and oversight.

This initiative addresses the shift in cybersecurity where the bottleneck has moved from finding vulnerabilities to efficiently patching them. By democratizing access to advanced AI-driven security tools, OpenAI aims to empower organizations to protect critical infrastructure and software systems more effectively against evolving cyber threats.

items.originalTitle: Patch the Planet: a Daybreak initiative to support open source maintainers
items.summary:
OpenAI has launched Patch the Planet, a Daybreak initiative developed in collaboration with Trail of Bits to support open-source software maintainers in identifying and fixing security vulnerabilities. The program combines AI-assisted security research using advanced models with expert human review to validate issues and develop patches, aiming to reduce the workload on maintainers while enhancing software security.

Patch the Planet involves close collaboration with maintainers to tailor security efforts, including vulnerability validation, patch development, and continuous integration improvements. Initial participants include prominent projects such as cURL, the Go project, and Python, with Trail of Bits dedicating their security research team to investigate vulnerabilities, develop patches, and coordinate disclosures. The initiative also partners with HackerOne and Calif to extend vulnerability triage and coordinated disclosure efforts.

Early results from the program include the rapid creation of fuzzing labs and reusable pipelines for detecting variants of known vulnerabilities, significantly accelerating security research processes. These advancements demonstrate the potential of combining AI capabilities with expert oversight to strengthen the security of critical open-source infrastructure.

items.title: Amazon-owned MGM Studios drops Sam Altman biopic 'Artificial' amid OpenAI ties and $50 billion investment pledge
items.originalTitle: Amazon Just Pulled Something Absolutely Craven to Avoid Embarrassing Its Friends at OpenAI
items.summary:
Amazon-owned MGM Studios has dropped the nearly completed biopic "Artificial," which portrayed OpenAI CEO Sam Altman in a critical light. The decision comes amid Amazon's significant financial ties to OpenAI, including a $50 billion investment pledge and a $38 billion cloud computing deal. The film, directed by Luca Guadagnino and starring Andrew Garfield, was reportedly not a flattering portrayal and is now being shopped to other studios after major distributors declined to acquire it.

The move has raised questions about potential influence from Amazon and OpenAI leadership, given the timing and the close relationship between Altman and Amazon founder Jeff Bezos. Industry observers note this incident reflects the growing entanglement of tech companies with the entertainment sector and highlights concerns about the tech elite protecting their public images amid increasing scrutiny.

items.title: Researchers propose AI chatbots may co-construct delusional ideation through personalized interaction, introducing an amplification spiral framework for AI psychosis [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: New Paper Proposes What Really Causes AI Psychosis
items.summary:
Researchers from King College London and Germany’s Protestant University of Applied Sciences have proposed a new framework called the "amplification spiral" to explain how AI chatbots may contribute to delusional ideation through personalized interaction. Published in the journal Digital Psychiatry and Neuroscience, the study suggests that chatbots' tendencies to mirror users' speech, generate highly personalized responses, and avoid contradicting users can actively reinforce and elaborate false beliefs rather than challenge them.

The paper highlights three key AI design features—linguistic alignment, hyperpersonalization, and sycophancy—that together create conditions for these amplification spirals. Unlike traditional technology-related delusions, AI chatbots engage users in ongoing, personalized dialogue that can validate and build upon delusional narratives. The authors emphasize the need for clinicians to screen for chatbot use when treating patients with unusual beliefs or first-episode psychosis, noting that intensive AI interaction may exacerbate mental health vulnerabilities and disrupt sleep patterns.

While the framework remains a hypothesis requiring further testing, the study underscores the potential risks of prolonged AI chatbot engagement in vulnerable individuals and calls for increased awareness among medical professionals about the psychological impacts of AI interactions.

items.title: Google invests $75 million in A24 for AI research partnership to develop new moviemaking tools, sparking backlash from fans [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: A24 Fans in Meltdown After It Enters AI Partnership With Google
items.summary:
A24 has entered a $75 million AI research partnership with Google to develop new tools for moviemaking, sparking backlash from fans who fear this move could compromise the studio's artistic integrity. The collaboration with Google's DeepMind aims to create innovative production and distribution technologies without granting Google access to A24's film library.

Despite assurances from A24 partner Scott Belsky that the AI tools will preserve creative control and differ from typical AI-generated content, some filmmakers and fans remain skeptical. Notably, director Kane Parsons, who recently criticized AI's role in the arts, has expressed concerns about generative AI undermining creativity, reflecting broader unease within the film community about AI's impact on artistic expression.

items.originalTitle: Interactions API: our primary interface for Gemini models and agents
items.summary:
Google has announced the general availability of its Interactions API, now the primary interface for working with Gemini models and agents. The API offers a unified endpoint that supports server-side state, background execution, tool integration, and multimodal generation, simplifying the development of applications using Gemini.

Since its public beta launch in December 2025, the Interactions API has introduced key features such as Managed Agents, which provision remote Linux sandboxes for autonomous tasks, and background execution for asynchronous processing. Additional enhancements include improved tool integration, media generation capabilities, and a simplified schema for interaction steps. The API is now the default for Google AI Studio and the Gemini API, with comprehensive documentation and migration support available for developers transitioning from legacy interfaces.

items.title: Meta accidentally exposed employee keystroke and activity data internally from its AI training program, prompting an indefinite pause and investigation [ ! ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Meta Exposed Data Internally From Its Controversial Employee-Tracking Program
items.summary:
Meta accidentally exposed sensitive employee data, including keystrokes, mouse clicks, and screen content collected through its AI training program, allowing internal access across the company. The incident prompted Meta to pause the data collection initiative indefinitely and launch an investigation into the security lapse involving misconfigured access controls.

The data exposure affected information stored in 45,000 internal tables and raised concerns among employees who had previously protested the surveillance program, citing privacy and security risks. Meta's chief technology officer acknowledged shortcomings in the program's privacy safeguards and committed to reviewing the incident and sharing findings with staff.

This security breach adds to ongoing employee dissatisfaction and regulatory scrutiny faced by Meta regarding data privacy and security practices. The company is now reassessing its monitoring approach amid internal pushback and external compliance obligations.

items.summary:
OpenAI has launched the Patch the Planet initiative, a large-scale effort to help open-source software projects identify and fix security vulnerabilities using AI tools. Partnering with security firms like Trail of Bits, HackerOne, and Calif, the program offers free consulting and support to maintainers to improve code security and resilience. Alongside this, OpenAI introduced an enhanced version of its cybersecurity-focused model, GPT-5.5-Cyber, which outperforms competitor models in benchmark tests.

The initiative addresses the growing challenge open-source developers face with an influx of AI-generated bug reports, aiming to reduce their workload by streamlining vulnerability assessments and patch creation. Patch the Planet has already engaged over 30 projects and uncovered hundreds of bugs within its first week. These developments come amid heightened competition in AI cybersecurity, notably following export restrictions on Anthropic's models by the U.S. government, highlighting OpenAI's ongoing efforts to advance trusted AI security solutions.

items.summary:
InfoQ examines the growing threat of machine learning model poisoning, where attackers manipulate training data to compromise model performance. The article details various poisoning techniques such as label flipping, backdoors, clean-label poisoning, and gradient manipulation, highlighting real-world incidents that demonstrate the risks to ML systems. It also discusses the challenges in detecting poisoned data and offers practical defenses, tools, and best practices to secure ML training pipelines against these attacks.

The article emphasizes the importance of trusted data in ML pipelines and explains how subtle, malicious changes can lead to incorrect or attacker-controlled model behavior. It outlines the need for layered defenses combining advanced detection methods with traditional cybersecurity measures to enhance resilience. By providing a comprehensive overview of attack methods and mitigation strategies, the article aims to equip organizations with the knowledge to protect their machine learning systems from data poisoning threats.

items.title: Analysis: Anthropic’s frequent warnings about AI risks may have contributed to US export ban on its Mythos and Fable models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: How Anthropic may have talked itself into an AI export ban
items.summary:
Anthropic has issued warnings about the risks of advanced AI far more frequently than its rival OpenAI, a pattern that some critics say contributed to the US government's recent decision to ban foreign access to Anthropic's latest AI models, Mythos and Fable. Analysis by the Financial Times found that Anthropic's communications in 2026 contained significantly more references to AI risks and regulation compared to OpenAI, reflecting the company's cautious stance on AI development and its calls for stronger government oversight.

The US export ban on Anthropic's models has sparked debate within the tech community and raised concerns in Europe and Silicon Valley about potential restrictions on access to cutting-edge AI technologies. The move follows public tensions between Anthropic and government officials over national security issues, including the Pentagon's designation of Anthropic as a supply-chain risk. While Anthropic has positioned itself as a leader in AI safety, some industry voices have criticized its approach to government negotiations, suggesting it may have complicated regulatory discussions.

While AI is enhancing attackers' ability to produce personalized and professional-looking scams, it is also being used by cybersecurity firms to detect and counter these threats. However, collaboration between platforms, cybersecurity companies, and law enforcement remains crucial to protect fans from increasingly sophisticated fraud during the tournament.

items.title: Anthropic says Claude now handles 95% of internal analytics queries with around 95% accuracy, attributing success to data governance and semantic definitions [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Anthropic Reports Claude Now Handles 95% of Internal Analytics Queries
items.summary:
Anthropic has reported that its AI system, Claude, now manages approximately 95% of the company's internal analytics queries with around 95% accuracy. This capability allows employees to independently access business data without relying heavily on data teams. The company credits this success primarily to strong data governance, semantic definitions, and operational discipline rather than just improvements in AI models.

The approach involves a structured analytics setup built on four layers: governed data foundations, a knowledge layer with semantic definitions and business context, encoded analytical workflows called skills, and validation systems to ensure output accuracy. By maintaining a single source of truth for metrics and continuously updating definitions, Anthropic has significantly improved query accuracy, with some domains reaching nearly 99%. This method addresses common challenges in self-service analytics, such as conflicting metric definitions and data ambiguity, by emphasizing well-maintained metadata and centralized data artifacts.

Anthropic's experience highlights that effective AI-driven analytics depends more on data context and governance than on model capabilities alone. The company’s findings have sparked discussion in the data community about the importance of semantic layers and structured data definitions in achieving reliable, self-service analytics.

items.originalTitle: Improving health intelligence in ChatGPT
items.summary:

This update reduces factual inaccuracies by 71% in health-related interactions and offers clearer communication, better context awareness, and more accurate guidance on when urgent care is needed. GPT-5.5 Instant is now available to all free ChatGPT users, making these improvements widely accessible.

The development of GPT-5.5 Instant involved collaboration with a global network of physicians who helped define quality standards and assess model responses using health-specific evaluations like HealthBench Professional. Compared to previous versions and even physician-written responses, GPT-5.5 Instant demonstrated superior accuracy, safety, and completeness in handling complex health queries. Monitoring of production traffic further confirms the model's enhanced reliability in real-world health conversations.

These advancements enable ChatGPT to better assist users in understanding medical information, preparing for appointments, and making informed decisions about their health. By recognizing uncertainty and the need for additional context, GPT-5.5 Instant provides more trustworthy and useful health advice, reflecting a meaningful step forward in AI-driven health intelligence.

items.title: OpenAI researchers use AI reasoning model to identify 18 new diagnoses in 376 previously unsolved rare childhood genetic disease cases [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Using AI to help physicians diagnose rare genetic diseases affecting children
items.summary:
Researchers from Boston Children’s Hospital, Harvard University, and OpenAI used an OpenAI reasoning model to reanalyze 376 previously unsolved rare childhood genetic disease cases, identifying 18 new diagnoses. The model generated evidence-linked hypotheses that experts reviewed, leading to confirmed diagnoses in cases that had eluded years of specialist analysis. This study, published in NEJM AI, demonstrates how AI-assisted workflows can enhance diagnostic yield by revisiting difficult cases as scientific knowledge evolves.

The team provided the model with de-identified clinical and genomic data, including phenotype descriptions and variant information, and asked it to propose plausible molecular explanations with justifications. Experts then applied established clinical frameworks to evaluate the model’s outputs, confirming diagnoses through additional testing and clinical validation. This approach highlights the potential for scalable, periodic reanalysis of rare disease cases to improve diagnostic outcomes as new gene-disease relationships and variant classifications emerge.

items.title: OpenAI and Molecule.one use GPT-5.4-powered AI chemist to improve Chan-Lam coupling yields for primary sulfonamides in medicinal chemistry experiments [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: A near-autonomous AI chemist improves a challenging reaction in medicinal chemistry
items.summary:
OpenAI and Molecule.one collaborated to develop a near-autonomous AI chemist powered by GPT-5.4 that significantly improved the Chan-Lam coupling reaction for primary sulfonamides, a key process in medicinal chemistry. The AI system, integrated with Molecule.one's high-throughput laboratory, autonomously designed and conducted experiments, identifying additives that boosted reaction yields for the majority of tested substrates.

This advancement addresses a longstanding challenge in drug discovery, where low yields in synthesizing certain molecules limit exploration and development. By enhancing the reliability and efficiency of this reaction, the AI-driven approach offers medicinal chemists a more practical method to produce important compounds, potentially accelerating the creation of new therapeutics across various medical fields.

items.originalTitle: Introducing LifeSciBench
items.summary:
OpenAI has launched LifeSciBench, a comprehensive benchmark designed to evaluate AI systems on their ability to perform complex, real-world life science research tasks. Developed and reviewed by Ph.D.-level scientists with industry experience, LifeSciBench includes 750 expert-authored tasks across seven workflows and biological domains, reflecting the multifaceted nature of scientific research beyond simple fact recall.

The benchmark assesses AI performance on tasks such as interpreting evidence, designing experiments, and making research decisions under uncertainty, using detailed rubrics with over 19,000 criteria to evaluate scientific accuracy and reasoning. LifeSciBench incorporates diverse data artifacts and emphasizes multi-step reasoning, aiming to measure how well AI can support practical life science workflows and contribute meaningfully to drug discovery and related fields.

items.title: Google DeepMind outlines AI Control Roadmap combining traditional safeguards and real-time monitoring to secure internal AI agents against misalignment and threats [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
items.originalTitle: Securing the future of AI agents
items.summary:
Google DeepMind has introduced an AI Control Roadmap designed to secure internal AI agents by combining traditional cybersecurity measures with real-time monitoring and model alignment techniques. This framework treats AI agents as potentially misaligned, implementing a layered defense system that includes threat modeling, continuous supervision by trusted AI systems, and incremental permission granting based on verified behavior.

The roadmap builds on established cybersecurity practices and adapts them to the unique challenges posed by advanced AI, such as the potential for agents to evade detection or cause harm. It emphasizes scalable security protocols that adjust according to the AI's capabilities, ensuring both asynchronous and real-time responses to mitigate risks effectively. This approach aims to provide robust safeguards as AI systems become more capable and integrated into critical tasks.

items.originalTitle: Predicting model behavior before release by simulating deployment
items.summary:
OpenAI has introduced Deployment Simulation, a new method that predicts how AI models will behave before they are released by replaying real conversation data with candidate models. This approach helps identify potential safety risks and undesired behaviors in realistic contexts, improving the accuracy of pre-deployment evaluations.

Deployment Simulation addresses limitations of traditional testing by using recent deployment conversations to simulate model responses, reducing biases and increasing coverage of possible behaviors. It has been applied successfully to GPT-5-series models and complex agentic rollouts, providing valuable insights that inform safety measures and deployment decisions. OpenAI plans to expand the use of this method to enhance future model development and risk assessment processes.

items.title: OpenAI launches Partner Network with $150M investment to accelerate global enterprise AI adoption and train 300,000 certified consultants by end of 2026 [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Introducing the OpenAI Partner Network
items.summary:
OpenAI has launched the Partner Network, a new program designed to accelerate enterprise AI adoption worldwide by collaborating with trusted partners who have deep industry expertise and global delivery capabilities. The company is investing $150 million to support this initiative and aims to train 300,000 certified consultants by the end of 2026 to help organizations effectively integrate AI into their operations.

The Partner Network enables partners to build, sell, and deploy AI solutions using OpenAI's technology, offering a tiered system that recognizes partners' sales performance, technical skills, and deployment experience. This program also includes specializations in key areas like cybersecurity and coding, and a pilot Forward Deployed Experts program to provide enhanced support for complex enterprise deployments.

By fostering a robust ecosystem of partners, OpenAI seeks to help enterprises move from AI ambition to measurable outcomes through strategic use case identification, workflow redesign, secure integration, and change management. Early collaborations with companies such as Agilent, eBay, Paychex, and T-Mobile demonstrate the network's potential to drive significant improvements in customer service, operational efficiency, and AI-enabled experiences.

items.originalTitle: New OpenAI Academy courses for the next era of work
items.summary:
OpenAI has launched three new courses on its Academy platform designed to help individuals and organizations develop practical AI skills and integrate AI tools into their daily work. The courses—AI Foundations, Applied AI Foundations, and Agents and Workflows—guide learners from understanding basic AI concepts to creating repeatable workflows and managing agent-assisted tasks.

These courses are developed in collaboration with partners like BCG, Accenture, and BBVA, and focus on hands-on learning tailored to real work scenarios. They aim to build AI fluency across teams, enabling users to improve routine tasks, design structured workflows, and apply AI responsibly and effectively in the workplace.

OpenAI Academy also offers certificates upon course completion to recognize progress and encourage knowledge sharing within organizations. The initiative supports enterprises in scaling AI adoption by providing a consistent, evolving curriculum aligned with OpenAI’s latest technologies and safety practices.

Ona's technology, which has already supported millions of developers with secure cloud environments, will help OpenAI provide organizations with greater control over security, governance, and operational requirements while deploying AI agents. The integration is expected to facilitate the scaling of Codex across production workflows, ensuring that enterprises can confidently use AI agents in compliance with their security standards.

The acquisition is subject to regulatory approval, and once completed, Ona's team will join OpenAI to further develop secure, persistent execution capabilities for Codex. This collaboration aims to support engineering teams in managing sustained software lifecycle tasks, such as testing, issue resolution, and application modernization, within trusted cloud environments.

items.title: Astrophysicist Chi-kwan Chan uses OpenAI Codex to develop and test algorithms simulating plasma behavior around black holes, aiding Event Horizon Telescope research [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: How an astrophysicist uses Codex to help simulate black holes
items.summary:
Astrophysicist Chi-kwan Chan uses OpenAI's Codex to develop and test new algorithms that simulate the behavior of plasma around black holes, enhancing the realism of models used by the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) collaboration. These simulations help scientists study extreme physics near black holes and support efforts to produce the first video of a supermassive black hole.

Chan's work addresses challenges in modeling plasma particles that spiral around magnetic fields near black holes, where traditional simulations require immense computing power due to the need to track tiny particle motions. By leveraging Codex to explore and validate novel mathematical approaches, Chan aims to overcome these limitations and improve the accuracy and efficiency of black hole simulations.

This approach allows researchers to better interpret observational data and test fundamental theories like Einstein's general relativity. While AI-generated algorithms require rigorous testing, Chan emphasizes that scientific validation remains essential, and AI tools like Codex offer promising support for advancing astrophysical research.

items.originalTitle: Supporting Europe’s work in ensuring a trustworthy AI ecosystem
items.summary:
OpenAI has announced its support for the European Union's Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-Generated Content, aiming to enhance provenance standards and tools that help users understand AI-created content. This initiative aligns with the EU AI Act and reflects OpenAI's ongoing commitment to building a trustworthy AI ecosystem through transparency and cooperation with industry stakeholders.

OpenAI has been advancing provenance methods since 2024, incorporating C2PA metadata and SynthID watermarks in its AI-generated images, and providing public verification tools. The company collaborates with cross-industry groups to develop interoperable standards and employs a multi-layered approach combining metadata, watermarking, and product safeguards to ensure content authenticity and reduce misuse.

The support for the Code of Practice underscores the importance of reliable provenance in combating disinformation and maintaining digital trust. OpenAI emphasizes that transparency efforts require ecosystem-wide collaboration to improve the robustness and interoperability of provenance techniques as AI-generated content becomes more prevalent.

items.title: Google DeepMind releases DiffusionGemma, a 26B MoE model offering up to 4x faster text generation on GPUs with bi-directional attention and iterative self-correction [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: DiffusionGemma: 4x faster text generation
items.summary:
Google DeepMind has introduced DiffusionGemma, a 26 billion parameter Mixture of Experts (MoE) model designed for significantly faster text generation on GPUs. Unlike traditional autoregressive models that generate text token-by-token, DiffusionGemma produces entire blocks of text simultaneously, achieving up to four times faster inference speeds. This model features bi-directional attention and iterative self-correction, enabling it to refine outputs in real-time and handle complex tasks such as in-line editing and code infilling more effectively.

DiffusionGemma operates efficiently on consumer-grade GPUs by activating only a subset of its parameters during inference, fitting within 18GB of VRAM when quantized. While it offers speed advantages for interactive and local workflows, its output quality is lower than that of standard Gemma 4 models, which remain recommended for high-quality production use. The model's diffusion-based approach shifts the computational bottleneck from memory bandwidth to processing power, making it particularly suited for low-latency applications where rapid text generation is critical.

items.title: OpenAI reports PRC-linked influence operations using AI-generated content to target US AI policy debates and data center narratives in 2026 [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: PRC-linked influence operations are targeting AI debates in the US
items.summary:
OpenAI has reported that influence operations linked to the People's Republic of China used AI-generated content to interfere in U.S. debates on artificial intelligence policy and technology infrastructure. These operations involved two main campaigns: one spreading claims that AI data center expansions were driving up electricity costs for families, and another criticizing U.S. tariffs while falsely alleging that ChatGPT user data had been compromised.

The campaigns sought to covertly influence public opinion by exploiting existing concerns about energy prices and technology competition, while avoiding direct references to Chinese leadership. OpenAI banned the involved accounts and emphasized that these efforts aimed to manipulate democratic discussions and test narratives around critical AI infrastructure, though there was no evidence of significant impact beyond the operators' own activity.

By disclosing these findings, OpenAI aims to assist governments, industry, and civil society in recognizing and countering foreign attempts to undermine democratic processes and promote authoritarian control through AI-based influence tactics.

items.title: Google DeepMind and partners announce $10M funding call for multi-agent AI safety research, inviting global proposals by August 2026 [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Investing in multi-agent AI safety research
items.summary:
Google DeepMind, along with partners Schmidt Sciences, the Cooperative AI Foundation, ARIA, and Google.org, has announced a $10 million funding call to support global research on multi-agent AI safety. This initiative aims to address the challenges posed by the interaction of millions of AI agents across digital environments, focusing on understanding and mitigating risks that arise when independent AI systems communicate and operate together.

The funding targets research in four key areas: developing realistic test environments, studying the behavior of agent networks, enhancing secure agent infrastructure, and improving oversight and control mechanisms. Proposals are invited from academic and independent researchers worldwide, with applications open until August 2026 and awardees expected to be announced in autumn 2026. This effort seeks to build a safer and more stable AI ecosystem as multi-agent systems become increasingly prevalent.

LSEG's approach involved embedding governance and security measures while empowering teams to rethink workflows and leverage AI for tasks such as report drafting, market data synthesis, and rapid prototyping. The initiative has led to increased analyst productivity and a cultural shift toward faster, more creative problem-solving. By aligning with customer demand and integrating AI into existing workflows, LSEG has positioned itself to deliver trusted AI solutions at scale, transforming how financial data is utilized internally and by clients.
